title: The Broken Homecoming
premise: Oscar Okafor has spent seventeen years keeping their head down in the town of Millbrook, where the Founders' Festival and its mysterious 'Hearth Loaf' tradition have defined life for generations. When a group chat of five classmates starts receiving messages predicting events days before they happen, Oscar discovers they can bake prophecies into bread — a gift inherited from the town's founders, who bound Millbrook's prosperity to an annual ritual that is secretly failing. As the predictions turn dark, Oscar and their unlikely found family must uncover what the founders really bargained for, confront the festival committee's corrupt chair who has been feeding the ritual lies to keep her power, and choose between preserving a broken tradition or baking a new one. In the end, Oscar remakes the Hearth Loaf with truth instead of control, saving the town not by restoring the old magic but by sharing it.
about_author: Hazel Joubert grew up above her grandmother's bakery in a small river town, where she learned that every recipe carries a story. She writes warm, strange stories about kids who find their people in the unlikeliest places.

chapters.title: Proofing
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Establishes Oscar's invisible-kid routine at Millbrook High and their gift: whatever feeling they knead into dough comes true in small ways for whoever eats it. They keep it secret, even from Dad. Emotional beat: loneliness disguised as safety, cracked when a loaf meant for comfort makes a classmate weep in the cafeteria.

chapters.title: The Chat Nobody Made
chapters.summary: Oscar is added to a group chat called 'Tomorrow' with four strangers: Priya, Dex, Marisol, and quiet Theo. The first message predicts a bus crash that happens exactly as described, down to the minute. POV alternates between Oscar and Priya. Emotional beat: terror braided with the electric thrill of finally being seen.

chapters.title: Five Strangers, One Recipe
chapters.summary: The five compare notes and discover each received a different fragment of an old recipe card — the Hearth Loaf, centerpiece of Millbrook's Founders' Festival. Oscar recognizes the handwriting as their late grandmother's. Emotional beat: reluctant alliance; Oscar wants out, but the second prediction names someone they love.

chapters.title: What the Festival Feeds
chapters.summary: Oscar and Theo sneak into the festival archive and learn the Hearth Loaf isn't symbolic: it renews a founding bargain each year, and the loaf baked last year was wrong. Committee chair Vivian Marsh watches them leave. Emotional beat: the vertigo of learning your hometown runs on something hidden and hungry.

chapters.title: Rising
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. The chat predicts a fire at the Okafor bakery; the five stage a near-miss rescue that saves Dad and exposes them to Marsh's suspicion. Dex confesses his family has served the committee for generations. Emotional beat: found family solidifying under pressure — five kids choosing each other over safety.

chapters.title: Marsh's Ledger
chapters.summary: Marisol hacks the committee's records: for thirty years, Marsh has substituted false ingredients and edited the ritual to concentrate the town's luck on her own ventures, starving whole neighborhoods. The predictions are the bargain fighting back. Emotional beat: righteous fury; power revealed as theft wearing tradition's clothes.

chapters.title: Sour
chapters.summary: Marsh frames Oscar for tampering with festival supplies; Dad's shop is shuttered, and the group fractures when Dex wavers, tempted by Marsh's offer to restore his family's standing. Oscar bakes despair by accident and nearly loses themselves. Emotional beat: the darkest hour — identity questioned, family scattered.

chapters.title: The Old Bargain
chapters.summary: Theo reveals he's a descendant of the founders and the chat was his doing — a plea for help he didn't know how to make alone. Together they read the original covenant: the founders never intended one keeper; they intended a table. Emotional beat: forgiveness and purpose; the prophecy was an invitation all along.

chapters.title: Festival Eve
chapters.summary: The five split up: Marisol leaks the ledger publicly, Priya and Dex stall Marsh's counterfeit loaf ceremony, while Oscar and Theo bake the true Hearth Loaf from the recovered recipe — kneading in grief, hope, and every neighbor's offered memory. Emotional beat: breathless convergence, everything staked on dough and trust.

chapters.title: Breaking Bread
chapters.summary: Climax and resolution. At the festival, Marsh forces a confrontation before the whole town; the false loaf crumbles, and Oscar offers the real one to everyone, ending the single-keeper bargain. The predictions stop; the magic becomes ordinary generosity. Oscar, no longer invisible, stands at a table full of chosen family. Emotional beat: belonging earned, power shared.
